name: Immich
summary: Immich is a self-hosted photo and video library: the phone app backs up the camera roll, the web app browses, searches and shares it. One immich-server image runs a NestJS API and a job worker that pull work from Valkey through BullMQ and keep everything in Postgres with the VectorChord vector extension; a separate Python service runs the CLIP, face and OCR models. Mapped read-only from the code; nothing was run.
facts: NestJS + Kysely · SvelteKit · Flutter · FastAPI + ONNX
docker compose: server, ML, Valkey, Postgres
16 Nov 2026 · fix: dev stack install race (#33377)
caveat: Read only, from a shallow clone at ff445d5: source, docker compose files, Dockerfiles and GitHub workflows. Nothing was installed, built or run, so every part is 'built' (in the code), none live. Not checked: the hardware-acceleration variants beyond their Dockerfile stages, iOS release steps, the plugin and workflow system, maintenance mode, and anything only the docs claim.

nodes.label: API clients (SDK)
nodes.what: The server writes an OpenAPI spec; oazapfts turns it into the @immich/sdk TypeScript client and openapi-generator into the Dart client the phone app uses. Generated files are never edited by hand.
nodes.state: In the code: packages/sdk/src/fetch-client.ts is generated (header says DO NOT MODIFY); the Dart client is generated into mobile/generated/openapi.

evidence.note: open-api task: sync spec, oazapfts TS SDK, Dart generator

nodes.label: Web app
nodes.what: The browser app: timeline, albums, search, people, sharing and admin. It is a static single-page build that talks to the API mostly through @immich/sdk (a few direct fetch calls) and listens for live events over socket.io.
nodes.state: In the code: built with adapter-static (fallback index.html) and copied into the server image at /build/www.

evidence.note: SvelteKit SPA, SSR off, talks through @immich/sdk

nodes.label: Mobile app
nodes.what: Backs up the phone's camera roll and browses the library. Uploads run as background tasks (background_downloader) that POST each file to /assets; a local Drift (SQLite) database keeps the synced state.
nodes.state: In the code: Flutter with Riverpod and Drift; the generated Dart OpenAPI client is a path dependency.

evidence.note: generated openapi client as a dependency

nodes.label: Immich CLI
nodes.what: A command-line tool for bulk uploads with an API key. It hashes files, asks the server which checksums it already has, then uploads the rest to /assets.
nodes.state: In the code: commands login, logout, server-info and upload; also bundled in the server image.

evidence.note: CLI copied into the server image

nodes.label: Auth
nodes.what: Every non-public request is checked here: a shared-link key or slug, a session token (header, bearer or cookie) or an API key (stored as a SHA-256 hash). OAuth sign-in uses OIDC discovery, with PKCE when the provider supports it.
nodes.state: In the code: AuthService.validate tries share key, share slug, session, then API key, else 401.

evidence.note: API key looked up by SHA-256 hash

nodes.label: API server
nodes.what: The REST API every client uses, on port 2283 under /api. It handles uploads, search, albums and sharing, pushes live events over socket.io, and serves the built web app. It queues background work instead of doing it.
nodes.state: In the code: the supervisor forks the API worker as a child process; ApiModule boots Express with sirv for the web files.

evidence.note: API worker forked; microservices as a worker thread
/api prefix, websocket adapter, web files via sirv

nodes.label: Job workers
nodes.what: Runs the background jobs. One BullMQ worker per queue hands each job to the service method marked @OnJob. Follow-up jobs are chained: when one succeeds, JobService.onDone queues the next (sidecar → metadata, storage template → thumbnails, thumbnails → smart search, faces, OCR, video), and StorageTemplateService queues the storage template job when metadata extraction finishes.
nodes.state: In the code: started as a worker thread in the same container by default; IMMICH_WORKERS_INCLUDE/EXCLUDE can split API and microservices.

evidence.note: microservices start workers; API only watches
run job, then onDone on success or skip

nodes.label: Media tools
nodes.what: The libraries the jobs call: sharp/libvips decodes images and writes previews, thumbnails and thumbhashes; fluent-ffmpeg probes and transcodes video; exiftool-vendored reads and writes metadata.
nodes.state: In the code: MediaRepository wraps sharp and ffmpeg; MetadataRepository wraps exiftool-vendored, which MetadataService calls to read tags.

evidence.note: thumbnail job: video via ffmpeg, image via sharp

nodes.label: Notifications
nodes.what: Turns events (album invite, album update, sign-up) into in-app notifications and, if the user wants them, rendered emails that a SendMail job sends over SMTP.
nodes.state: In the code: email rendered with react-email and sent with nodemailer; skipped unless SMTP is enabled in the admin settings.

evidence.note: album invite: in-app notice, render email, queue SendMail
SendMail job, skipped if SMTP disabled

nodes.label: External library sync
nodes.what: Imports photos that live in folders Immich does not own. One microservices instance takes a lock, schedules the library scan cron and watches the import paths; new files become assets and go through the same metadata jobs.
nodes.state: In the code: feature-frozen (bug fixes only, per AGENTS.md).

nodes.label: ML service
nodes.what: A separate Python service with one /predict endpoint. Each request names the task and model; it loads the model (cached, unloaded after a TTL) and returns CLIP embeddings, faces with embeddings, or OCR text.
nodes.state: In the code: separate image immich-machine-learning, with GPU variants (cuda, rocm, openvino, armnn, rknn). The server reaches it at http://immich-machine-learning:3003 by default.

evidence.note: model from cache with ttl, loaded on demand
M-CLIP, InsightFace and PaddleOCR model names

nodes.label: OIDC provider
nodes.what: An identity provider the admin can point Immich at for single sign-on. Immich discovers it from the issuer URL and runs the authorization-code flow.
nodes.state: In the code: openid-client discovery, authorizationCodeGrant; off unless configured.

nodes.label: Hugging Face
nodes.what: Where the ML service downloads its ONNX models on first use, from the immich-app organisation, into its model cache volume.
nodes.state: In the code: snapshot_download from settings.model_organization (default immich-app).

nodes.label: SMTP server
nodes.what: Any mail server the admin configures; Immich sends notification emails through it with nodemailer.
nodes.state: In the code: transport built per send from the SMTP settings; verified when the config is saved.

evidence.note: nodemailer sendMail with the configured transport

nodes.label: Media storage
nodes.what: One host folder mounted at /data holds everything Immich writes: upload/ (new originals), library/ (after the storage template), thumbs/, encoded-video/, profile/ and backups/.
nodes.state: In the code: the compose file mounts UPLOAD_LOCATION; StorageCore builds nested paths per user.

nodes.label: Postgres
nodes.what: All metadata: users, assets, EXIF, albums, shared links, faces, people and system config, through Kysely. The VectorChord (or pgvector) extension stores CLIP and face embeddings in smart_search and face_search and answers nearest-neighbour queries; earthdistance does offline reverse geocoding.
nodes.state: In the code: compose uses an immich-app postgres 14 image with vectorchord 0.4.3; the server picks vchord first, then vector.

evidence.note: vector extensions and the two vector tables
reverse geocode with earth_distance in SQL

nodes.label: Valkey (Redis)
nodes.what: The job queue: BullMQ keeps one queue per job type under the immich_bull prefix. The same Redis-protocol server also fans out socket.io events between workers.
nodes.state: In the code: compose runs valkey:9; jobs default to one attempt, removed on success, kept on failure.

evidence.note: BullMQ config: prefix immich_bull, one queue per name

nodes.label: External libraries
nodes.what: Folders the admin adds as import paths. Immich reads the files where they are instead of copying them into its own storage.
nodes.state: In the code: a file watcher on importPaths with exclusion patterns; paths validated before use.

evidence.note: sync job imports files as assets

nodes.label: GitHub Actions
nodes.what: CI builds the server and ML images on pushes to main, release branches, PRs and published releases; separate workflows bump the version, cut the release branch, build the signed Android app and draft the release.
nodes.state: In the code: .github/workflows/docker.yml, prepare-release.yml, draft-release.yml, build-mobile.yml.

nodes.label: Container images
nodes.what: immich-server and immich-machine-learning images (plus -cuda, -openvino, -armnn, -rknn, -rocm ML variants) on GitHub Container Registry, tagged by version, commit and 'release'; stable releases are mirrored to Docker Hub.
nodes.state: In the code: tag rules in docker.yml; compose pulls ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-server:${IMMICH_VERSION:-release}.

evidence.note: mirror to Docker Hub on stable release

nodes.state: In the code: draft-release.yml creates the draft with these files; publish is a separate gated job.

features.name: A phone photo becomes searchable
features.line: From the phone's backup to a stored file, extracted metadata, thumbnails, a CLIP vector and indexed faces.
steps: im-mobile
The backup service builds an UploadTask and POSTs the file as multipart assetData to /assets, in the background.
im-api

The upload route checks the user's permission and quota; multer has already written the file under upload/<user>; the asset row is created with its SHA-1 checksum and an AssetExtractMetadata job is queued.

steps.note: access, quota, create row, queue job

steps: im-redis
BullMQ holds the job in the metadata-extraction queue until a microservices worker picks it up.
im-workers
exiftool reads dates, size, GPS (reverse-geocoded against Postgres), then the storage template job runs and, when it finishes, thumbnail generation is queued.
im-media
sharp writes the preview, thumbnail and thumbhash; on success smart search, face detection and OCR jobs are queued and the clients get an on_upload_success event.

steps.note: queue SmartSearch, faces, OCR; notify clients

steps: im-ml
The preview goes to /predict three times by default: a CLIP image embedding, face boxes plus face embeddings, and OCR text.

steps.note: OCR on the preview (on by default)

steps: im-db
The CLIP vector is upserted into smart_search and new faces into face_search; new faces queue facial recognition. The photo now answers smart searches.

features.name: A smart search
features.line: Typing 'beach at sunset' finds photos by meaning, not by tags.
steps: im-web
The search page calls searchSmart from @immich/sdk when smart search is on, with the user's language.
im-api
POST /search/smart checks smart search is enabled and works out which users' photos may be searched.
im-ml
The query text is encoded by the CLIP text model (cached per model, query and language).
im-db
Postgres orders smart_search rows by vector distance (<=>) through the VectorChord index and returns one page.
im-web
The results come back as assets and albums and the page renders them.

features.name: Faces become people
features.line: Detected faces are clustered into people by embedding distance, without anyone tagging them.
steps: im-workers
The face detection job sends the preview to the ML service unless facial recognition is off or the asset is hidden.
im-ml
InsightFace detects faces and returns a box and an embedding for each.
im-db
New faces and their embeddings are saved; each new face gets a FacialRecognition job.
im-workers
Recognition searches face_search for neighbours within maxDistance; with at least minFaces matches it joins an existing person or creates a new person group, otherwise it is deferred.
im-media
A new person gets a thumbnail job that crops the face from the original photo (the preview for videos).

steps.note: person thumbnail input: original, or preview for video

features.name: A video is transcoded
features.line: Videos that browsers can't play are re-encoded with ffmpeg, with hardware acceleration if set.
steps: im-workers
After thumbnails, a video asset also gets an AssetEncodeVideo job.
im-media
The job decides the target from the ffmpeg settings; if nothing needs changing it skips, otherwise ffmpeg runs, falling back to software if hardware acceleration fails.
im-disk
The result is written to encoded-video/<user>/xx/yy/<id>.mp4 and recorded as the asset's encoded file.
im-api
Playback serves the encoded file if there is one, else the original, with byte-range support.
im-web
The browser's video element loads /assets/:id/video/playback (or an HLS stream when real-time transcoding is on).

steps.note: video src: playback path or HLS stream

features.name: Sharing an album link
features.line: An owner makes a link; anyone with it can open the album without an account.
steps: im-web
The owner creates a shared link for an album (optional password, expiry, upload and download switches).
im-api
The service checks AlbumShare permission and always creates the link with a random 50-byte key, plus an optional custom slug.
im-db
The link is stored; a clashing slug is rejected by a unique constraint.
im-web
A visitor opens /share/<key>; the page loads the link with getMySharedLink.
im-auth
The key is looked up and accepted unless the link has expired; the request then acts as the link.
im-api
Thumbnails and videos are served on routes that allow shared-link auth.

features.name: A release ships
features.line: A version bump becomes container images, a GitHub release and an Android build.
steps: im-actions
Prepare release bumps the version, commits it and cuts a release/vX.Y branch.
im-release
Draft release tags the branch, builds and signs the Android app and drafts a release with the compose files, example.env and APK.
im-actions
When the release is published, the Docker workflow builds immich-server and every ML variant.
im-ghcr
Images are pushed to ghcr.io with version and 'release' tags, and stable ones are mirrored to Docker Hub.
im-api
A self-hoster's compose file resolves immich-server:${IMMICH_VERSION:-release} (example.env pins the v3 tag); the new version runs once they docker compose pull and up -d.
